title: Top Seven Discoveries in the K-Field Domain

discoveries.name: Independent Cell3 geometric reconstruction
discoveries.summary: Multiple independent astronomical analysis methods converge on the same three-plane, non-orthogonal, globally oriented Cell3 geometry.
discoveries.significance: Establishes the geometric foundation from observational data without prior physical assumptions.

discoveries.name: ICRS orientation lock
discoveries.summary: The K-Field exhibits a fixed global orientation in the ICRS/J2000.0 frame defined by a primordial normal vector.
discoveries.significance: Introduces an absolute directional reference for physical processes.

discoveries.name: Mass Bridge closure
discoveries.summary: Cell3 face-area ratios reproduce key dimensionless physical constants using a shared geometric carrier.
discoveries.significance: Links mass and electromagnetic scales through a single geometric structure.

discoveries.name: Reciprocal metric interaction hierarchy
discoveries.summary: The inverse metric reveals a strongly ordered interaction structure |I_bc| >> |I_ac| >> |I_ab|.
discoveries.significance: Demonstrates that interaction strengths are encoded in geometric dual space.

discoveries.name: Lucas-limit emergence
discoveries.summary: Shared-face repetition of Cell3 produces a minimal higher-order structure exposing polarity and internal layering.
discoveries.significance: Reveals hidden structural organization beyond a single cell.

discoveries.name: Seven-sheet polarity system
discoveries.summary: The Lucas-limit structure resolves into seven alternating-polarity sheets forming a coherent modulation system.
discoveries.significance: Introduces an internal layered system capable of generating directional and phase behavior.

discoveries.name: Cross-domain convergence
discoveries.summary: The same K-Field geometry and orientation organize both astronomical structures and laboratory observations.
discoveries.significance: Demonstrates that one framework spans multiple physical scales and observational domains.
